verify.cmd: node -e 'const fs=require("fs");const r="lib/nav/member-event-rewrite.ts",p="proxy.ts",pub="app/(public)/events/[slug]/page.tsx";for(const f of [r,p,pub])if(!fs.existsSync(f))process.exit(79);const rw=fs.readFileSync(r,"utf8"),px=fs.readFileSync(p,"utf8"),pb=fs.readFileSync(pub,"utf8");const gatesOnSignInAlone=/if\s*\(\s*!signedIn\s*\)\s*return null/.test(rw);const proxyPassesClaim=/memberEventRewrite\([^)]*claim/.test(px);const publicReadsClaim=/claim/.test(pb);if(gatesOnSignInAlone&&!proxyPassesClaim&&!publicReadsClaim){console.error("SCAN-799: a signed-out organizer on /events/<slug>?claim=<token> is served the public ISR body, which never reads the claim flag, so the Claim This Event banner never appears.");process.exit(1)}'

append.detail: The outreach claim link resolves to /events/<slug>?claim=<token>, but lib/nav/member-event-rewrite.ts returned null for every signed-out request, so proxy.ts served a signed-out organizer the cookie-free ISR body under app/(public), which never reads ?claim and never shows the Claim This Event banner (a regression from the SCAN-636 public split). memberEventRewrite now takes a third hasClaim flag and gates on (!signedIn && !hasClaim); proxy.ts passes request.nextUrl.searchParams.has('claim'), so a claim-link visit is rewritten to the member page, whose existing banner already verifies the token against the row and routes a signed-out organizer into /join with a next= return. x-pathname stays the share path, so the (main) layout still renders that visitor in public chrome, and every other anonymous request keeps the ISR body. Pinned by lib/nav/member-event-rewrite.test.ts: a signed-out visitor with ?claim is rewritten to /full, one without stays on the ISR path, and the reserved slugs and sub-routes still never rewrite even with the flag.
